chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding a man who arrives from his journey during the time of prayer, he said: 'If he does not fear that the time will expire, let him complete [the prayer]; and if he fears the time will expire, let him shorten [the prayer].'
ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do with his prayer if he arrives just as the prayer time begins?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the flexibility in prayer duration for travelers, prioritizing the certainty of praying within its time over the completeness of the prayer structure. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'ease in hardship' (taysir), allowing the traveler to choose between performing the full four-rak'ah prayer if time permits or shortening it to two rak'ahs to ensure the prayer is not missed entirely. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining ritual integrity and accommodating the practical constraints of travel.
